report.summary: At the 17:40:19 restart the pool shrank from 10 connections (30 s timeout) to 2 (250 ms). An idle-in-transaction session then held locks, exhausting the pool; transfers failed with 500/503 or were slow.

findings.claim: A restart at 17:40:19 cut poolMaximumSize 10→2 and poolConnectionTimeoutMs 30000→250.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed pool settings starting at the restart inside the window.

findings.claim: The tiny pool timed out: 161 acquisition timeouts, with pending/active borrowers at the cap of 2 from 17:40:23 on.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts at the 250 ms limit and saturation starting right after the restart.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session (81908) blocked two ledger_app sessions from 17:40:22 to 17:41:26, holding the 2 connections and worsening the exhaustion.
findings.reason: Blocked sessions were seen in 28-30 samples, max wait ~2 s, matching the pool saturation period.

findings.claim: Transfers show 57×500 and 104×503 (25.6% server errors) and p95 1.7 s. Outbox arrivals and publications dropped in the buckets covering the restart and blocking.
findings.reason: The error and throughput collapse coincide with the pool and blocking window; E1 and E2 are not split by time, so this is the timing link rather than a direct per-error attribution.

limitations: Metrics have a 10 s scrape gap at 17:40:13–17:40:23 and 16 NaN gauge samples, so the restart moment is poorly observed.
